p: One agent
The same agent, the same models and the same account in every place it runs.
Install
Linux, macOS and Windows. Dev updates itself the way it was installed.

code: dev login # pick an account: Hanzo is the default dev login --hanzo # straight to your Hanzo account dev login --with-api-key # or paste a Hanzo API key, hidden

p: Models

h2: Enso by default. Any model by name.

p: Dev starts on enso-auto through api.hanzo.ai, so every call is metered on your Hanzo account. Every model Hanzo serves is a flag or a /model away.

code: dev # enso-auto, through api.hanzo.ai dev --model enso-ultra # name any model Hanzo serves /model zen5-coder # or switch inside a session

p: Controller
Kai is Dev’s own controller, not an adviser. At each step it returns an operation Dev can run, or says plainly that it abstains. The cheapest step that holds is the one taken.
Proof
Nothing counts as done because a model said so.
Sandbox
Commands run in a sandbox and are approved inside it. Ask before every action, or lift the fence for one run. A repository’s own tool servers stay off until you say you trust it.

code: hanzo dev --ask # ask before each action hanzo dev --no-sandbox # run unconfined, for this run only hanzo dev --project-mcp # also load this repository's .mcp.json

p: Gen

h2: Dev is our agent. Gen runs any agent.

p: Hanzo Gen is the harness: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and the rest, on Hanzo’s tools and models and linked to your account. Dev is the agent it opens when none is named.
Open source
Dev is Apache-2.0 on GitHub. Build it, change it, send a pull request — hanzoai/dev .
